title: Printable
description:
Teach `std::cout` how to print a `Vec2`: write `operator<<` so that `std::cout << Vec2{ 1.5, 2 }` prints `(1.5, 2)`.

The left operand is the stream, the right operand is your object, and the function must **return the stream** so that `<<` can be chained.
hints: The signature is `std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& out, const Vec2& v)`. Write the parts to `out` and finish with `return out;`, so `<<` can continue after it.
unitTests:
TEST("prints in brackets") { std::ostringstream out; out << Vec2{ 1.5, 2 }; CHECK_EQ(out.str(), "(1.5, 2)"); }
TEST("chains with other output") { std::ostringstream out; out << "from " << Vec2{ 0, 0 } << " to " << Vec2{ -3, 4 } << '!'; CHECK_EQ(out.str(), "from (0, 0) to (-3, 4)!"); }
